A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LAT study, with readable main text, equations, figures, and appendices. The impact statement, trojan examples, and normalization analysis can be matched across their relocations.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Figures 2–5 report original image-classification, text-classification, and text-generation experiments, including adversarial robustness and trojan removal.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical experiments and adds reported transformer-layer comparisons in Appendix C and Figure 6.

M1.justification: The core LAT procedure and architectures remain unchanged, but Equation (3) changes the normalized perturbation from δ · max(σ, α) to max(δ · σ, α). This specifies a different transformation; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed accordingly.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet, Redwood injurious text, Anthropic-HH, and BeaverTails for the same tasks and attack/trojan scenarios. The added layer sweep uses retained text-classification coverage; newly cited jailbreak techniques are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set remains input-space or embedding-space AT and random latent perturbations, including their normalized counterparts. Newly cited methods, such as Xhonneux et al. (2024), are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v4 adds area-under-Pareto-curve summaries and describes activation-relative perturbation bounds for the newly reported layer sweep. Section 4.1 also changes the stated ImageNet evaluation split from validation to test, without establishing that different images were used or experiments rerun.

E4.justification: v1 mentions preliminary layer selection without displaying its results. Appendix C and Figure 6 in v4 add a systematic DeBERTa layer-sensitivity comparison, supporting early layers and layer 3 specifically. The normalization comparison and harmful-training analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C newly specifies that layer-sweep ROC-AUC results are averaged across three training runs. v1 describes multiple runs with varying perturbation bounds but gives no corresponding averaging count. No confidence intervals, seed identifiers, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: v4 newly reports LAT-versus-AT Pareto-area improvement summaries of 68%, 68%, and 1.5% for image attack, patch-trojan, and natural-feature-trojan evaluations, and 1.1% and 1.0% for text attack and trojan evaluations. It also adds layer-wise results. The principal rankings remain, including AT's advantage on BeaverTails trojan removal; rescaled axes do not establish gains over v1.

T1.justification: Equation (3), moved from Appendix A to Appendix D, changes mathematically: the minimum α moves from the standard-deviation scaling factor to the scaled perturbation itself. These expressions are not equivalent. The main minimax objectives remain equivalent, and neither version adds theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that LAT can address failures without triggering examples, usually improve clean/robust tradeoffs relative to AT, and sometimes worsen robustness. The added quantitative support and revised emphasis do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v4 recasts the layer-selection limitation as broader unpredictability and configuration effort, adding difficulty interpreting and choosing perturbation magnitude. It also explicitly proposes future machine-unlearning applications. The model-scale limitation, absence of jailbreak evaluation, and dataset-dependent trojan interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly states that RLP perturbations match LAT's norm, documents the layer sweep's activation-relative bound, and acknowledges compute from the Center for AI Safety. The trojan examples and code-access information were already present in v1; their relocation is not new reproducibility content.

R1.justification: Related work expands to include many-shot and image jailbreaks, unforeseen-attack robustness, and continuous-attack training, including Anil et al. (2024), Bailey et al. (2023), Dai et al. (2022), and Xhonneux et al. (2024). DEF CON and OpenAI red-teaming references are removed. The central positioning of LAT remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and several paragraphs are rewritten, Section 4 gains explanatory signposts, and the impact statement and trojan footnotes move into appendices. The main section sequence remains. v4 also introduces proofreading defects, including raw BibTeX embedded in the BeaverTails reference.

P2.justification: Figures 2–4 and the normalization figure switch from delta axes to absolute-valued axes, although the main captions still describe changes. v4 adds the layer-sweep Figure 6, renumbers the normalization display to Figure 7, resizes Figure 1, and adjusts captions, legends, and spacing.

improvement.justification: v4 provides useful evidence for layer selection, averages that analysis across three runs, and quantifies existing Pareto comparisons. However, it introduces an unexplained, non-equivalent normalization equation and inconsistencies between plotted axes and captions. These gains coexist with reduced clarity about the specified method and results, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
